questions.question: What is the core invariant for a reliable API contract?
options: Every endpoint uses the same URL shape
The same valid request and documented preconditions have predictable success, failure, and retry meaning
All endpoints return 200 for successful work
Clients never need to upgrade
questions.explanation: A reliable contract lets a caller predict what a valid request, failure, and retry mean. Naming and transport support that promise but do not replace it.

questions.question: A client times out after POST /payments. Which retry is safest when the server supports idempotency keys?
options: Send the same body with a new key
Retry with the same caller-scoped key and request fingerprint
Retry repeatedly without a key until a 201 arrives
Change POST to GET
questions.explanation: The same key and request fingerprint let the server recognize one logical payment and replay its stored result instead of creating another payment.

questions.question: Why must authorization be enforced at the resource boundary, not only by a gateway token check?
options: A token always proves a caller owns every resource
The service must verify that this identity may act on this specific tenant and payment
Gateway authentication makes logging unnecessary
It makes pagination faster
questions.explanation: Authentication identifies a caller. Resource authorization proves that the identified caller has permission for the particular resource and operation.

questions.question: Which collection contract prevents a client from causing an unbounded history response?
options: An opaque cursor, stable ordering, maximum page size, and continuation metadata
An offset with no maximum limit
Returning every record so clients do not need another request
Using a generic 500 error when the result is large
questions.explanation: A bounded cursor contract lets the server control work and payload size while giving the client a clear way to continue.

questions.question: Which change is safest for existing v1 consumers?
options: Rename a required response field in v1 immediately
Change a retryable error into a final error without notice
Add an optional field while preserving current semantics
Remove the old endpoint during the first v2 deployment
questions.explanation: Additive changes that preserve existing semantics are normally backward compatible. Behavior and required-field changes need an explicit migration path.

questions.question: What should a structured API error provide to a caller?
options: Only a stack trace so the caller can debug the server
A stable status and machine code, safe detail, correlation ID, and documented retry behavior
A different free-form message for each endpoint
A 200 status with an error hidden in success data
questions.explanation: A stable error contract helps callers recover safely and gives operators a correlation handle without exposing internal implementation details.
